candidate_relations.reason: The histopathology shows concentric perivascular proliferation of ovoid cells with SMA positivity and negative h-caldesmon, desmin, and smooth muscle myosin, consistent with myopericytic differentiation rather than endothelial differentiation. Angiosarcoma would show endothelial marker positivity (CD31/CD34 in tumor cells) and lacks the concentric perivascular SMA-positive pattern. CD31 here highlights pre-existing vascular channels, not the tumor cells themselves. The IHC profile and morphology support malignant myopericytoma, not angiosarcoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Angiosarcoma is a vascular malignancy but of endothelial origin, whereas malignant myopericytoma is a perivascular myoid tumor; both can occur on the scalp but represent distinct diagnostic entities with different histogenesis and IHC profiles

case_quality_flags: Classic malignant myopericytoma case with characteristic perivascular concentric growth, SMA positivity, and negative smooth muscle markers (h-caldesmon, desmin) distinguishing it from smooth muscle tumors and angiosarcoma
